summary: Phases 1-6 complete. The concurrent model-building segfault is fixed by a fail-fast, thread-reentrant single-threaded-construction guard raising ConcurrentConstructionError; validated by 60/60 isolated subprocess runs (three batches of 20) against a 5/8 and 6/6 pre-fix crash baseline. Regression sweep is clean: 2154 passed, 0 failed, 41 deselected vs a 2137/0/43 baseline, with every delta accounted for. Phase 7 (removing the -m "not slow" quarantine) is hard-blocked on task 136 and was deliberately not attempted; code/pyproject.toml is untouched.

blockers.description: Phase 7 (delete the -m "not slow" clause from code/pyproject.toml addopts) is gated on task 136 (ground_wallclock_performance_budgets), whose status in specs/state.json is 'not_started'. The quarantine clause covers two independent defects: the two interpreter-crashing concurrency tests (fixed by this task) and three ungrounded wall-clock budget assertions (owned by task 136). One of those three, tests/integration/test_performance.py::TestExecutionPerformance::test_simple_model_performance, was observed failing again in Phase 6 at 1.09s against its 1.0s budget. Removing the quarantine now would re-break the default run. Unblock by completing task 136, then run Phase 7: delete the clause, delete the TEMPORARY comment block at code/pyproject.toml:85-103, update the 'slow' marker description, and run the unfiltered suite 3 times as separate invocations requiring an identical green result set.

decisions_made: Phase 4's 60 subprocess samples were run with the oracle suite still active rather than deferred: those runs judge process exit codes only and assert no wall-clock, so CPU contention cannot skew them, and contention is a stronger probe for a scheduling-dependent race than an idle machine.

Phase 6 additionally ran the wider 'code/tests/ code/src/model_checker/' scope because the documented baseline in KNOWN_TEST_FAILURES.md was measured at that scope; the plan's literal narrower 'code/tests/' command alone could not support the baseline comparison it was asked to support. Both were run and recorded.

The bimodal BM_CM_4 full-suite failure was classified as the pre-existing load-sensitive flake, not a regression, on the evidence that it passes in isolation at 21.39s against a 30s budget and passed in the full-scope sweep.
Phase 7 was not attempted and code/pyproject.toml was left untouched, per the plan's own gate and the dispatch instruction.
